subsystems.role: collects enough infrared light from the planet to split into a spectrum.

subsystems.name: Light-curve processing

subsystems.role: infers which gases could produce the observed spectrum.

subsystems.name: Interior and tidal models
subsystems.role: test whether tidal heating could plausibly drive the observed activity.

buildSteps.title: Choose a target
buildSteps.detail: Pick a small rocky planet that transits a small, cool star, where a single transit blocks enough starlight to be measured, and where orbital eccentricity or resonance predicts real tidal heating.

buildSteps.title: Measure the star and the orbit
buildSteps.detail: Radial-velocity observations give the planet's mass; long photometric baselines give its radius, period and eccentricity, which set how much tidal energy is dissipated inside it.

buildSteps.title: Observe transits
buildSteps.detail: Record the star's light during transits, when starlight filters through any atmosphere, using near-infrared spectroscopy over many transits to build up signal-to-noise.

buildSteps.title: Observe eclipses
buildSteps.detail: Record the dip when the planet passes behind the star; the size of that dip gives the dayside temperature, so an excess reveals hot, freshly erupted surface.

buildSteps.title: Clean the data
buildSteps.detail: Fit and remove instrument drifts, detector systematics, stellar variability and unocculted starspots, which otherwise mimic a planetary signal.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve a composition
buildSteps.detail: Compare the corrected spectrum against model atmospheres to estimate abundances of sulphur-bearing gases and their uncertainties.

buildSteps.title: Test alternative sources
buildSteps.detail: Model ultraviolet-driven photochemistry: on a hydrogen-rich planet, sulphur dioxide can be made from hydrogen sulphide high in the atmosphere without any volcano.

buildSteps.title: Check replenishment
buildSteps.detail: Sulphur dioxide is destroyed by ultraviolet light within years, so model whether the observed amount requires a continuous surface source.

buildSteps.title: Confirm with repeat observations
buildSteps.detail: Only repeated, independent detections of the same species and a matching thermal excess justify calling a planet volcanically active.

prerequisites.tech: Space infrared spectroscopy at transit depth precision
prerequisites.why: JWST can measure the roughly one-part-in-a-thousand signals involved and has already detected sulphur dioxide on a gas giant.

prerequisites.tech: Precise masses and radii for small planets
prerequisites.why: mass, and therefore interior and tidal heating estimates, remain poorly constrained for most small planets.
sulphur reaction networks in hot, irradiated atmospheres are still uncertain, weakening the volcanic interpretation.
predicting how much a given planet outgasses requires assumptions about mantle rheology that are hard to test.

prerequisites.tech: A sample of suitable small, bright, transiting rocky planets
prerequisites.why: very few worlds combine small size, a small host star and an eccentric, tidally heated orbit.

pathway.milestone: tentative volcanic or outgassing signatures reported for a tidally heated Earth-sized world, alongside JWST spectra of hot lava worlds
pathway.unlocks: a first, disputed foothold in comparative planetology of rocky worlds.

pathway.milestone: repeat transit and eclipse observations confirming or refuting sulphur species on the best candidates
pathway.unlocks: separation of genuine volcanism from photochemistry and stellar contamination.

pathway.milestone: a small survey of rocky planets spanning a range of tidal heating rates
pathway.unlocks: a relationship between orbit, heating and observed activity.

pathway.milestone: larger space telescopes and extremely large ground telescopes resolving cooler, less irradiated rocky planets
pathway.unlocks: volcanism as a probe of interior state and long-term habitability.
